question: Article 148(5)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2026/1739 exempts milk supplied by a member to their cooperative from the requirement for a written contract where the cooperative’s statutes or derived rules contain transparent, democratically decided rules, which are made known in advance, on price determination and payment. Paragraph 7 provides a right to require a written contract for exemptions under paragraphs 5(b) and 6, but not under paragraph 5(a). 1.
Does revised Article 148 apply to milk delivered on or after 19 August 2028 where the governing agreement between the member and the cooperative was concluded before that date?

Is any competent authority required to verify that a cooperative meets the conditions set out in Article 148(5)(a), and what effective remedy is available to a member where those conditions are not met?

Does the transparency requirement in Article 148(5)(a) also cover the measurement of the volume, composition and quality of the milk on which a member’s payment is calculated? If not, does the Commission intend to address independent verification of such measurements through implementing acts under paragraph 11?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.11.2026) Following the entry into force and application of relevant provisions of the amended Common Markets Organisation (CMO) Regulation1, both existing and new agreements will need to comply with revised provisions on contracts, as from 19 August 2028. It is for Member States to ensure the correct application of the Regulation.

In parallel, pursuant to Article 3(1)(f) of the Unfair Trading Practices Directive2, national enforcement authorities are competent to investigate refusals to confirm the terms of supply agreements in writing.

While written confirmation is generally not required for deliveries by members to their cooperatives, enforcement authorities may investigate whether the conditions for this exception, as set out in the Directive, are met.

While recognising the important role played by cooperatives in strengthening farmers’ position in the supply chain, new Article 148(5)(a) of the CMO Regulation aims to ensure transparency in how members’ remuneration is determined. Rules on price determination should therefore enable members to understand how the price they receive is calculated, including how relevant factors may influence it.
At this stage, the Commission does not envisage further action through implementing acts in this area.
1 Regulation (EU) 2026/1739 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 July 2026 amending

Regulations (EU) No 1308/2013, (EU) 2021/2115 and (EU) 2021/2116 as regards the strengthening of the position of farmers in the food supply chain, OJ L, 2026/1739, 29.7.2026. 2 Directive (EU) 2019/633 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 April 2019 on unfair trading practices in business-to-business relationships in the agricultural and food supply chain, OJ L 111, 25.4.2019, pp. 59.
